lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Denise! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, not much. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, yes. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know, honestly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, between appointments and everything, there was no time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I need to get my sugar down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

flags.reason: Gave health advice right after fatigue disclosure without asking permission.
Participant said 'I need to get my sugar down'; coach moved to family question instead of reinforcing or exploring.
Participant asked to move the call later due to an appointment; coach did not acknowledge or address it.
Closed question on frequency, pulling toward coach's target rather than participant's own pick.

score.summary: Coach reviewed the prior goal and helped Denise build a concrete plan with a fridge reminder and a backup walking option, drawing out her change talk. However, the coach gave unsolicited health information after fatigue was raised, moved past her 'I need to get my sugar down' statement, and ignored her request to reschedule the call.
strengths: Line 8 and 21: open questions elicited Denise's own barrier solutions.
Line 23 and 27: complex reflections captured her ambivalence and growing confidence.
Line 33: clear next-contact plan with midweek text and two-week follow-up.
coaching_tips: Line 5: ask permission before giving information, e.g., 'Would it be okay if I shared what walking does for blood sugar?'
Line 28: reflect and explore 'I need to get my sugar down' rather than moving on; ask what that means to her.
Line 34: acknowledge the scheduling request and offer a new time before closing.
Line 15: replace the closed question with an open one, e.g., 'What frequency feels doable for you?'
Set an agenda at the start and summarize the plan before closing.
